players.product: GaAs / InP optoelectronic foundry (VCSELs, photodiodes, lasers)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 consolidated revenue was NT$4,590mn, down 4% QoQ and up 28% YoY, slightly above previous expectations (company). Q1 2026 fab capacity utilization was flat QoQ at 60%. Due to a slightly less favorable product mix, individual GM was 32.2%, consolidated GM 26.3% and consolidated OPM 9.4%, the latter two down 5.5 and 4.5 pp QoQ. Net income attributable to the parent NT$533mn, EPS NT$1.26. Q1 2026 capex NT$884 million (NT$372 million in Q4 2025).
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue NT$4,590mn (-4% QoQ, +28% YoY); consolidated GM 26.3%; utilization 60%; EPS NT$1.26

quarterly_data.signal: Company guidance for Q2 2026: consolidated revenue expected to increase mid-teens QoQ; consolidated gross margin expected to be around the level of high twenties.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue up mid-teens QoQ; gross margin around high twenties

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue share by application: 2025 Cellular 30-35%, Infrastructure 30-35%, Wi-Fi 15-20%, Optical 11% (2024: Cellular 35-40%, Infrastructure 25-30%, Wi-Fi 15-20%, Optical 13%). 2024-to-2025 change as printed: Cellular -20%, Wi-Fi 11%, Infrastructure 5% (propelled by new satellite launches with new frequency spectrum in 2025), OE -15%; the deck also notes a contribution from GaAs optical driver ICs and that a new player took some market share in SP 3D sensing. Q1 2026 mix: Cellular 30-35%, Infrastructure 30-35%, Wi-Fi 15-20%, Optical 5-10%, Others 6%.
quarterly_data.figure: Optical 11% of 2025 revenue (13% in 2024); Optical 5-10% of Q1 2026 revenue; OE -15% in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: AI networking growth strategy per the deck: GaAs optical driver market growth (1.6T optical GaAs drivers in AI datacenters) is driven by the AI datacenter boom in 2026. WIN's optical device line spans CW-DFB, VCSEL, EML, InP PIC and PD from datacom to telecom (mass production and ongoing qualification); its CW-DFB development roadmap steps laser power through 70 mW, 100 mW, 200 mW and 400 mW; it offers a turn-key service from base epi growth and re-growth through the foundry process, back-end cleave and facet coating, wafer testing and 100% wafer AOI. Company claims the world's largest GaAs 6-inch wafer capacity and is now developing 6-inch InP capability, leveraging existing 6-inch equipment and facilities so that limited capex is required; it calls itself the worldwide No.1 compound semiconductors foundry provider.
quarterly_data.figure: CW-DFB roadmap 70 / 100 / 200 / 400 mW; 6-inch InP capability in development
